chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Isma'il ibn Aban, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, raising it from Abu al-Mu'tamar who said:

I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any Muslim who serves a group of Muslims, Allah will give him the like of their number as servants in Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for serving other Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes serving the faithful as a direct path to divine honor, with Imam Ali (AS) transmitting the Prophet’s promise of reciprocal service in Paradise. It underscores the Shia emphasis on humility and communal service as acts of worship that elevate one’s spiritual status, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of mutual care among believers.
